name: Composite fingerprint (FingerprintJS, CreepJS)
plain: Combines dozens of signals into one visitor ID that survives cookie clearing.
meaning: Open and commercial libraries hash 50 to 100 signals, then match drifting fingerprints to past visitors. Research found 90% of fingerprints are unique on desktop but breaking up over weeks, so linking needs ML.

steps: Collect canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, screen, timezone, hardware
Server matches new IDs to old ones with ML

data.metric: 128-bit visitorId; open source version about 40 to 60 percent browser-ID accuracy per vendor claims, commercial claims 99.5%

limits.headline: Can combine many device traits into one visitor ID that survives cleared cookies
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, and again on each visit
can: Collect about 50 to 100 small traits about your device and browser
Merge them into one visitor ID
Match your new profile to an old one when a few traits change
Link your visits across days without any cookie
cannot: Be sure it is you, since many devices on desktop look alike or change after updates
See your name unless you log in
Match you well when Tor Browser or Brave hide or blur the traits
limits.differs: Fingerprints work better on desktop. Phones of the same model look more alike, so they are harder to tell apart.

story.what_it_is: A script combines dozens of small browser and device traits into one ID that survives cookie clearing.
story.for_you: You see no sign of it. Your browser quietly answers dozens of small questions, and the combined answers are often unique enough to pick you out of millions of people.
story.for_makers: Tools like FingerprintJS and CreepJS package this as a product. Sellers use it to stop fraud, fake accounts and refund abuse. It is also used to track people across sites when cookies are blocked.

use_cases.example: An online bank uses a visitor ID to see that a login came from a device never seen with this customer.
A retailer catches one person using many accounts to abuse a first order discount.
A free to play browser game stops a banned cheater from simply opening a new account.
A checkout provider scores each order partly by how familiar the device is.
An ad network tries to link anonymous browsing across sites after the person clears cookies.
A dating site blocks scam accounts that keep coming back from the same laptop.
A research page, Cover Your Tracks, shows how unique your browser is so you can see what leaks.

technical_bounds: Mobile devices are far less unique than desktop
Browser anti-fingerprint modes create noisy or common values

value.abuse: Cross-site tracking when third-party script is on many sites

linkedin.how: LinkedIn's script collects fingerprint signals; see research/linkedin-case.md

history.change: Hiding in the Crowd: 33.6% of 2M fingerprints unique, mobile less
FP-Stalker: fingerprints drift, linking gives average tracking duration up to 51.8 days
Private Browsing noise makes composite IDs unstable
Fingerprint protection default for known scripts

refs.label: Gomez-Boix et al., Hiding in the Crowd (WWW 2018)
